doc.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022

title: Mick, Keith, Ronnie Wood and jazz fan Charlie Watts
summary: Ries has known the band for 23 years; he recalls Charlie Watts's hotel room drawings and going to hear jazz together.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Anything that would surprise us about Mick and Keith Richards?

You know it’s like well luckily I’ve known them now for 23 years so it’s like as I said, they’re really prepared, I mean you know Keith has a guitar in his hand all the time and they’re always like working on stuff, new songs, they’re constantly writing, so and he’s reading books you know, Ronnie Wood — he’s like a great artist and he’s painting all the time. Charlie Watts who was a huge jazz fan you know, he actually also was an artist and so he has these beautiful sketches that whenever he got to a hotel when we flew to a different city he would arrive and the first thing he would do before he did anything else was unpack and then he would do a drawing of the room where he was, of that hotel. And then the view out of the window. So I’m sure there’s thousands and thousands of these and I luckily got to see some of these which are amazing. I hope that one day maybe there’ll be a gallery that’ll show these. So besides his love for jazz and so I probably hung out with Charlie more than anybody because we were just jazz freaks so we would go out and have dinner and then go hear some music in a city to hear jazz and then often I would set up a gig and he would come and play with me. So it was great. And you get to know their kids and their grandkids and their wives. So it’s this big family but it’s a great production but also it’s a big traveling family. It’s very special. It’s a really unique situation and luckily I feel close to them in a way, as close as you can to people who are so famous. You know? Like, but it’s in a very inviting, relaxed vibe and they keep, luckily knock on wood they’ve had me back all these years and so it’s been great to have this gig for so long.
